# U05 — The force preparation, then inlining through upstream's inliner, its component pipeline only where it inlined

Mandatory findings: F-pass-6 F-pass-9

## Permitted outcome

1. **The force preparation** (R06, C3.3). `idr-inline` first applies
   `ForceAtCapture`, then `ForceOfOneConstant`, to the module, from
   `IDR/Transforms/Inline/Prepare.cpp`, through the greedy driver with
   its changed flag, and invalidates what either rewrite left stale
   before any decision or graph is taken. Neither is a canonicalization
   pattern any more. Mandatory.
2. **`idr-inline` on `mlir::Inliner` with a component pipeline that runs
   only where an iteration inlined** (R22, F-pass-6, F-pass-9). The
   pipeline `canonicalize,cse` runs through `Pass::runPipeline` on a
   callable after an iteration inlined into it and on no other, so a do
   block still unfolds in one round, and the round's parallel function
   step stays the one canonicalization of every function nothing was
   inlined into. Its rows nest under `idr-inline` in `-mlir-timing`.
   Mandatory.
3. **`idr::InlineDecisions`**: the MLton rule as an analysis under the
   pass manager, reading `References` through the manager, its
   per-function part built in parallel, its components from
   `idr::stronglyConnected` (C2.1, R11, R14). It decides exactly as
   today. Mandatory.
4. **The facts.** The clone callback calls `into.absorb(callee)` (R01);
   the capture function gets its first facts through the accessors
   (R29); no call the preparation makes carries effects (R07).
   Mandatory.
5. **The pass obeys C2.0 and C2.1.** No symbol table of its own, no
   fingerprint, no state on the instance; preservation from what the
   pass knows it did; the inliner and its call graph are skipped in a
   run with no call to an inlinable function. Mandatory.
6. **The layout** (C1.1, R10). `IDR/Transforms/Inline/Inline.cpp` and
   `IDR/Transforms/Inline/Prepare.cpp` in library `IdrInline`, declared
   in `INC/Transforms/Inline.h`; `IDR/Analysis/Inline.cpp` and
   `INC/Analysis/Inline.h` in `IdrAnalysis`; `IDR/Inline` deleted,
   its `CMakeLists.txt` with it. Mandatory.

Consumer adaptations: none outside the write set. The round (U04) and
the tools (U14) construct the pass by the generated
`idr::createIdrInline()`. The dialect's copies of the two patterns go in
U01's units; the fixtures that state them under `--idr-inline` are
U21's.

## Fixed decisions

**Files and includes** (C1.1, R10). Every `.cpp` includes
`idr/IR/IdrDialect.h` first, then its area's header, then the `idr/`
headers it names, then MLIR and LLVM headers by name.

- `INC/Transforms/Inline.h`: includes `idr/Transforms/Passes.h.inc`
  with `GEN_PASS_DECL_IDRINLINE`, and declares, in namespace
  `idr::inlining` (`inline` is a keyword), the three entry points
  below. It forward-declares `idr::References` and includes no analysis
  header.
- `IDR/Transforms/Inline/Prepare.cpp` (`IdrInline`): the two patterns in
  an anonymous namespace and the three entry points. Includes
  `idr/IR/IdrDialect.h`, `idr/Transforms/Inline.h`, `idr/IR/Grades.h`,
  `idr/Analysis/References.h`, `mlir/IR/Matchers.h`,
  `mlir/IR/PatternMatch.h`, `mlir/IR/SymbolTable.h`,
  `mlir/IR/Threading.h`, `mlir/Transforms/GreedyPatternRewriteDriver.h`.
- `IDR/Transforms/Inline/Inline.cpp` (`IdrInline`): the pass, nothing
  exported; `GEN_PASS_DEF_IDRINLINE`. Includes `idr/IR/IdrDialect.h`,
  `idr/Transforms/Inline.h`, `idr/Analysis/Inline.h`,
  `idr/Analysis/References.h`, `idr/Analysis/Holds.h`,
  `idr/IR/TypeGraph.h`, `idr/IR/Layout.h`, `mlir/Analysis/CallGraph.h`,
  `mlir/Pass/PassManager.h`, `mlir/Transforms/Inliner.h`,
  `mlir/Transforms/Passes.h`.
- `INC/Analysis/Inline.h`, `IDR/Analysis/Inline.cpp` (`IdrAnalysis`):
  `idr::InlineDecisions`. The `.cpp` includes `idr/IR/IdrDialect.h`,
  `idr/Analysis/Inline.h`, `idr/Analysis/References.h`,
  `idr/Support/Scc.h`, `mlir/IR/Threading.h`.
- Each unit stays under 400 lines.

**The entry points** (`INC/Transforms/Inline.h`):

```cpp
namespace idr {
class References;
namespace inlining {
// The functions whose body forces its one suspension argument and returns
// the value: the wrappers ForceAtCapture looks for.
llvm::SmallVector<idr::FuncOp> forceWrappers(mlir::ModuleOp module);
// ForceAtCapture on every closure that names a wrapper; true when it rewrote.
bool forceAtCapture(mlir::ModuleOp module, mlir::SymbolTable &symbols,
                    llvm::ArrayRef<idr::FuncOp> wrappers);
// ForceOfOneConstant on every force of a one-use closure constant the sites
// list; true when it rewrote.
bool forceOfOneConstant(mlir::ModuleOp module, const idr::References &references);
} // namespace inlining
} // namespace idr
```

**`forceWrappers`** reads only the head of each function:
`module.getOps<idr::FuncOp>()`, a body of one block whose ops are
exactly an `idr.force` of a block argument and an `idr.return` of its
result (`Lazy.cc:175-193`). It walks no body.

**`forceAtCapture`** finds its roots, then runs the pattern on them.

- The roots: the functions into a `SmallVector` in module order; a
  `DenseSet<StringAttr>` of the wrappers' names; `mlir::parallelFor`
  over the function indices, each walking its own body and appending
  every `idr.closure` whose callee is in the set to its own slot; the
  slots concatenated in module order. The parallel part reads the IR
  and writes only its slot.
- The pattern is `Lazy.cc:170-256` over `idr::FuncOp`,
  `idr::ReturnOp`, `idr::ClosureOp`, `idr::SuspendOp`, with these
  changes. Every lookup is `symbols.lookup<idr::FuncOp>(name)`. The
  function is created by the rewriter before the wrapper, then entered
  with `symbols.insert(fn)`, which renames a collision and records it,
  and the new closure names `fn.getSymNameAttr()` as `insert` left it.
  Its name is `<wrapper>.capture<n>` (C6.3, R31), `n` the count of
  captures this run made for that wrapper plus one. It is private, with
  `setTotal(callee.getTotal())` and `setEffectsAttr(callee.getEffectsAttr())`
  and no `instance`, `clone`, `no_inline` or `break_last` (R29); its
  location is the wrapper's, as today. The reuse of a capture is a
  `DenseMap` from (wrapper, argument index, callee) to the function,
  local to the run; no name is read back (C6.3).
- The run state (the table, the reuse map, the counts) is one struct
  local to `forceAtCapture`; the pattern holds a reference to it.
- The driver: `applyOpPatternsGreedily` on the roots, with a
  `GreedyRewriteConfig` whose scope is the module's body region,
  strictness `ExistingAndNewOps` (a closure the rewrite builds, or one
  in a copied body, may match again, as a chain of wrappers does),
  folding off, constant CSE off, region simplification off, and the
  `changed` out-parameter as the result. A fold or a region rewrite
  would report a change that no analysis needs dropped and that the
  round's canonicalize makes anyway. A run that does not converge
  leaves valid IR, as today (`Lazy.cc:350`).

**`forceOfOneConstant`** needs no walk and no lookup.

- The roots come from `references`: for each function, each site whose
  `at` is `ConstantLike` with one result of one use, that use the
  suspension operand of an `idr.force`. Each root's label is the site's
  `target`, kept in a run-local `DenseMap` from the force to the label.
- `mayRunWithin(label, holder)` is equality of the two functions'
  components in `references.components()`, numbered once per run into a
  `DenseMap<Operation *, unsigned>` when there is a root; a label
  absent from the map names nothing. The holder names the label (the
  constant is one of its sites), so the label reaches the holder
  exactly when the two share a component. This is the walk R06 names,
  answered without walking; `Lazy.cc:67-88`'s search goes.
- The pattern is `Lazy.cc:96-128` over `idr::FuncOp` and `idr::CallOp`,
  with the label from the map (it fails unless the closure's callee is
  the label's name), the new `idr.call` built with no `effects`
  (R07: no old call, so none; the next `idr-effects` writes it), and the
  constant erased by the pattern once its one use is gone, so the
  `References` taken next sees no stale site.
- The driver: `applyOpPatternsGreedily` on the forces, scope the
  module's body region, strictness `ExistingOps`, folding, constant CSE
  and region simplification off, the `changed` flag as the result.

**`idr::InlineDecisions`** (`INC/Analysis/Inline.h`):

```cpp
class InlineDecisions {
public:
  InlineDecisions(mlir::Operation *module, mlir::AnalysisManager &am);
  bool isInvalidated(const mlir::AnalysisManager::PreservedAnalyses &pa) const;
  // The idr.func the rule lets the inliner inline.
  const llvm::DenseSet<mlir::Operation *> &inlined() const;
  unsigned inlinable() const;      // how many
  unsigned leaves() const;         // of those, how many the leaf rule took
  unsigned inlinableCalls() const; // idr.call sites whose callee is inlined
private:
  llvm::DenseSet<mlir::Operation *> chosen;
  unsigned leafCount = 0;
  unsigned callCount = 0;
};
```

The constructor takes `am.getAnalysis<References>()` and builds no
`References` and no `SymbolTable`. `isInvalidated` returns
`!pa.isPreserved<InlineDecisions>() || !pa.isPreserved<References>()`
(C2.1). The three numbers keep their names, values and comments
(`Decisions.cppm:13-15`, `:29-40`): 40, 60, 320.

**The decisions, in three phases** (`Decisions.cppm:41-97`, unchanged
in meaning, R22).

1. Per function, in parallel: `mlir::parallelFor` over the indices of
   `references.functions()`, skipping an external one, into one slot
   each: the targets of its `idr.call` sites but a self call, in walk
   order with repeats (`:59-67`); the targets of its other sites, self
   included (`:69`); the edges, one per target at its first call, none
   to a `no_inline` target (`:53-66`); whether it calls itself. A slot
   reads `references` and the targets' `no_inline`, and writes only
   itself.
2. Serially, in module order: the call count of each target is the sum
   over the slots (a count lands on another function, so it is merged,
   not written in parallel). The components are
   `idr::stronglyConnected<idr::FuncOp>(functions, edges)`, callees
   first; the order depends on module order and first-call order alone.
3. Serially, over the components: one of two or more is skipped; a
   function with `no_inline` or a self call is skipped; otherwise its
   size is `references.ops(fn)` plus, for each call site whose target is
   already chosen, that target's size less one; a leaf
   (`!references.hasCall(fn)`) of at most 40 ops is chosen; any other
   function is chosen when `(calls - 1) * (size - 60) <= 320`. Last,
   `callCount` sums, over the slots, the call targets that were chosen.

A function on a cycle is never chosen: `idr-loop-breakers` marks a
`no_inline` function on every cycle of references (C1.3), every edge
into one is dropped, and a cycle the components still find is skipped,
as today. The inliner's own `shouldInline` refuses a self-recursive
target and a target that is an ancestor of the call besides.

**The pass, in order.** Anchored on `ModuleOp`, a step of the round
only (C1.3, C3.2). `kept` below is a `PreservedAnalyses` holding
`SymbolTable`, `idr::Holds`, `idr::TypeGraph` and `idr::Layouts`: the
preparation changes no `idr.data` or `idr.ctor` and inserts symbols only
through the `SymbolTable` analysis, so C2.1's obligations keep exactly
these.

1. `wrappers = inlining::forceWrappers(module)`. When it is not empty,
   `captured = inlining::forceAtCapture(module, getAnalysis<SymbolTable>(), wrappers)`.
   When `captured`, `getAnalysisManager().invalidate(kept)`: the
   manager may hold analyses from before the capture functions existed.
   No reference to the table is used after this point.
2. `References &references = getAnalysis<References>()`;
   `forced = inlining::forceOfOneConstant(module, references)`. When
   `forced`, `getAnalysisManager().invalidate(kept)`, and `references`
   is not used again. This is C3.3's clear: the one after step 1
   already happened before `References` was taken, so a second one for
   `captured` would rebuild a current analysis.
3. `InlineDecisions &decisions = getAnalysis<InlineDecisions>()`;
   `numInlinable += decisions.inlinable()`,
   `numLeaves += decisions.leaves()`.
4. When `decisions.inlinableCalls()` is zero, nothing can be inlined:
   no iteration inlines, so no function is marked and no pipeline runs.
   The pass takes no `CallGraph` and builds no `Inliner`; it preserves
   as the table below says and returns. This is the common case of the
   rounds that reach the fixpoint.
5. The plain values the inliner reads: `inlinable`, a copy of
   `decisions.inlined()`; `marks`, a `DenseMap<Operation *, bool>` with
   an entry `false` for every `idr.func` of `module.getOps<idr::FuncOp>()`;
   `inlinedAny = false`. No analysis of ours is read once the inliner
   starts (C2.0, R15).
6. `InlinerConfig config`, with exactly:
   - `setDefaultPipeline(componentPipeline)`, `static void
     componentPipeline(OpPassManager &pm)` adding
     `createCanonicalizerPass()` then `createCSEPass()` with their
     defaults (C3.2). Every callable is an `idr.func`, so the inliner's
     one pipeline per op name is anchored there.
   - `setMaxInliningIterations(std::numeric_limits<unsigned>::max())`:
     a component's iterations end when one inlines nothing; the
     decisions, taken once from the sizes, bound the growth. A do block
     of n statements needs n iterations in one round
     (`Round.cppm:12-18`).
   - `setCloneCallback`, wrapping `config.getCloneCallback()` as
     `Pass.cc:51-59` does: `into` is the `idr.func` that owns
     `inlineBlock` (the op itself or its nearest such parent); `callee`
     is `dyn_cast<idr::FuncOp>(src->getParentOp())`. When `into` is
     found: `into.absorb(callee)`, its entry in `marks` set (found, never
     inserted), `inlinedAny = true`. Then the default clone.
   - Not set: `setOpPipelines`; the multiple-blocks setter (the
     inliner's own test, with the carried patch of PINS.md
     `inline-unreachable`, decides a callee that ends in
     `ub.unreachable`).
7. The profitability callback is `Pass.cc:60-63` over
   `inlinable.contains(region->getParentOp())`.
8. The pipeline runner, the `RunPipelineHelperTy` the inliner calls,
   is a lambda capturing `this` and `marks`:

   ```cpp
   // A function nothing was inlined into is as the round's function step
   // left it; canonicalizing it again would cost a serial walk of it.
   auto runner = [this, &marks](Pass &, OpPassManager &pipeline, Operation *op) -> LogicalResult {
     auto it = marks.find(op);
     if (it == marks.end() || !it->second)
       return success();
     it->second = false;
     return runPipeline(pipeline, op);
   };
   ```

   The inliner calls it from its workers, one callable each, during an
   optimization phase; the clone callback runs on the pass thread
   during the sequential inlining phase. A runner finds its own entry
   and writes only its value; nothing inserts into `marks` once the
   inliner starts, so the map never rehashes under a reader.
   `runPipeline` runs the pipeline with the verifier after each pass and
   the manager's instrumentation, so `Canonicalizer` and `CSE` nest
   under `idr-inline` in `-mlir-timing` (with the carried patch of
   PINS.md `pass-timing-dynamic-pipeline`) and C8.2's zones open. A
   `PassManager` built inside the pass would have none of that.
9. `CallGraph &graph = getAnalysis<CallGraph>()`, as upstream's pass
   takes it, after the preparation and its invalidation, so it holds
   the capture functions. The runner runs a pipeline on a function
   nested in the module, which runs under that function's nested
   manager (recalled: the dynamic pipeline callback nests the manager
   for an op other than the pass's own), so the module's analyses, the
   graph included, stand while the inliner holds it. No pass but
   `idr-inline` computes a `CallGraph`.
10. `Inliner inliner(module, graph, *this, getAnalysisManager(), runner,
    config, profitable)`; a failed `doInlining()` is
    `signalPassFailure()`.

**Preservation** (C2.0, C2.1). The pass never measures the module to
find out what it did.

| The run | Preserved |
| --- | --- |
| no rewrite by the preparation, inliner skipped or inlined nothing | everything (`markAllAnalysesPreserved()`) |
| the preparation rewrote, inliner skipped or inlined nothing | `SymbolTable`, `Holds`, `TypeGraph`, `Layouts`, `References`, `InlineDecisions` |
| `inlinedAny` | `Holds`, `TypeGraph`, `Layouts` |

`References` and `InlineDecisions` in the second row were taken after
the last invalidation, so they are current. "Inlined nothing" rests on
two facts of the pinned inliner: it erases only callables an inlining
left dead, and with no mark set the runner ran nothing. Once anything
was inlined, the component pipeline may have rewritten any marked body
and the inliner may have erased functions without the `SymbolTable`
analysis, so only the three declaration analyses are claimed.

**What each round costs here.** Walks removed: the two fingerprints of
the module (`Pass.cc:74`, `:79`); the module-wide greedy run of
`ForceAtCapture` (`Lazy.cc:347-351`), now a read of function heads and,
only when a wrapper exists, one parallel walk to collect roots; the
symbol-use walk of a body at each step of `mayRunWithin`
(`Lazy.cc:83`), now a component compare; `ForceOfOneConstant` tried on
every force by every module canonicalize, now tried once per run on the
roots `References` lists; the `References` and `SymbolTable` built in
place (`Decisions.cppm:42`, `Pass.cc:34`), now the manager's; the
`CallGraph` and the inliner in a run with no inlinable call. What stays
serial: the decisions' merge and rule (linear in the sites), the
upstream `CallGraph` and use-list construction, the inliner's
component order, and the component pipeline across components (upstream
optimizes one component at a time, in parallel only within it). These
are the serial residue R47 records.

**Dependent dialects.** `getDependentDialects` builds `OpPassManager
pm(idr::FuncOp::getOperationName())`, calls `componentPipeline(pm)` and
`pm.getDependentDialects(registry)`: a dynamically run pipeline's
dialects are loaded before the manager runs, and the pipeline says
which. The `cf.br` the inliner's block form of `idr.return` makes is the
idr dialect's dependency (C1.2, R22).

**State.** The run-local structs of `Prepare.cpp`, the slots of the
decisions, `inlinable`, `marks` and `inlinedAny` live for one run. Nothing
is `thread_local`, `static` mutable, `std::atomic` or a member of the
pass (C1.1).

  (`Lazy.cc:38-88`) have no successor: the table, `insert` and the

- `T/idr/pipeline/do-block` (U21, on `idr.func`): the 16 `put_str` stay
  in order, no call is left in `@Main.main`,
  `idr-expect=holds=no-closures` holds, and `fixpoint: round {{[1-3]}}
  changed nothing` (`do-block.mlir:14-33`). This is F-pass-6's property
  under F-pass-9's rule: the canonicalize that follows an iteration on
  the function it inlined into turns the apply of the next thunk into a
  call the next iteration inlines. The coordinator's sensitivity run
  shows it failing at 25890d32.

## Escalate if

- A capture function made in an earlier round is not reused. C6.3
  forbids reading a name back, and none of C1.2's facts keys a capture,
  so this part reuses one only within a run (`Lazy.cc:217-221` reused
  one across runs by name). A later round may make a second copy for
  the same wrapper, argument and callee, which `symbol-dce` erases once
  nothing names it. Report whether the coordinator wants a key on the
  function that would allow reuse across rounds; no ruling settles it.

## Binding rules

1. Do exactly the assigned obligations and necessary consumer adaptations within the exclusive write set. Every changed hunk, new file, dependency or abstraction must map to a named obligation. If the contract cannot be completed within those writes, report the exact missing seam; do not silently widen scope.
2. Add no unsolicited features, frameworks, generic helpers, configuration knobs, retries, telemetry, documentation, dependencies, formatting sweeps or neighboring cleanup. Elegance means completing the selected representation and deleting its named predecessor, not opening another project.
3. Do not be afraid to duplicate reading, investigation, reasoning or small packet-local non-authoritative implementation glue. Do not wait for a sibling merely to avoid that duplication or introduce a shared helper that creates a false dependency. Reuse already-landed repairs; duplicated investigation does not mean rebuilding working mechanisms.
4. Authoritative schemas, vocabularies, identities and business facts still have exactly one owner. Never duplicate them, create competing implementations or write concurrently to another owner's file. Duplicate effort is allowed; duplicate authority and overlapping writes are not.
5. Finish the bounded deliverable, report changed paths against obligations plus checks actually run and unresolved seams, then return control. Do not roam into another packet, manufacture work to maintain swarm headcount, or build a reporting/coordination platform.
6. User steering goes through the coordinator into the affected packet only. The coordinator corrects an architectural contradiction in the canonical contract and re-dispatches the affected lane. No lane stops for it.
